52 hours in and I’m still surprised by how much I’m enjoying Escape From Duckov. On the surface it looks like a goofy duck parody of Escape From Tarkov, but underneath the memes is a genuinely solid top-down extraction shooter. Each raid is a tight loop of scouting, sneaking, looting, and trying to reach an extraction before the zone chews you up.

The risk/reward balance is great: pushing deeper into the post-apocalyptic maps for better loot always feels tempting, especially with the day/night cycle and weather events shaking things up. Quests and traders give you clear goals between runs, and the crafting/progression systems make new gear feel like an actual upgrade instead of just another skin.

What really surprised me is the amount of support building up around the game already: interactive community maps, drop-rate tracking, and even mods like a third-person shoulder camera if you want a more traditional shooter feel. It all makes the core game even more replayable.

If you want something with the tension of an extraction game but wrapped in a lighter, funnier package (and starring heavily armed ducks), this is absolutely worth your time. Easy recommend.

[h2]Escape from Duckov is the benchmark.[/h2]
This is where the mechanics of escaping from a conflict zone came into perfection. It isn't just PVE - it's a world where every decision impacts your survival. Every raid is a unique scenario. You go in taking risks and come out with the spoils, or don't come out at all.

[h2]Realistic character manipulation, ballistics, advanced armor system, bleedings - this is not just another shooter game.[/h2]
It's a simulation of combat in extreme conditions. Everything has a price: armor, ammo, time. A mistake in a raid means losing everything. Trading, crafting, hideout, barters, skill leveling, completing tasks - these are not side objectives, they are the basis of progress. The winner is not the one who shoots better, but the one who lives in the world of Duckov, understands the intricacies and has a strategic advantage.

[h2]Infinite comibations of sights, gadgets, and accessories to create unique builds[/h2]
Countless models of equipment and weapons, brought as close to reality as possible. Character appearance customization, clothing for different seasons - all this affects the gameplay and your chances of survival.

[h2]Each location means a different tactic, different pace, different risk[/h2]
Factory plants, forests, city districts. No repetitiveness. You never know what awaits you in a new raid. Night raids, bad weather, gunfights, unique Bosses - every raid could become your last. But after dying in a raid, you can't give up. You learn from your mistakes and re-equip your character to try to grasp and escape from Duckov once for all.

Short version: Game kills you in unfair and poorly designed ways, or due to bugs and you lose hours and hours of progress, kind of like if I deleted your save when you went on a bathroom break. Skip it if you value your time. 

Long version:
If you value your time, then skip this one. The game will gladly evaporate hours of loot for deaths that aren't even your fault. For example, there's a certain area in the game that you have to get a ticket to get to and if you die in that area, even if it is because of a bug, crash, or something else, you will lose ALL of the loot you have on you. For someone busy like me with a high earning career, the stress this adds to the stress I already get from my job simply is not worth the effort. I absolutely fell in love with this game when the demo was available, the full release adds so much to the game.

This is a fantastic isometric extraction shooter with heaps of content. Through my entire playtime (91 hours at time of review) I never got bored or or felt the game was getting too repetitive. The maps all have their own distinct charm and reason to go back to them, from the small easy going starter map, to the massive scope of Farm Town and beyond. Each situation and map lends itself to different weapons, encouraging you to try out different tactics and gear combinations to find something that meshes well for you. The quests are varied and interesting, from basic things like kill X number of Y type of enemy with Z weapon to solving spooky mysteries, hauling cargo from one map to another or catching certain fish. Quest progression feels nice and allows for continuous unlocks of new weapons/armor/attachments/stims and even some mini-games. The game can be stressful at times but not in a bad way. The plethora of difficulty options let you tailor your game experience to match your skill level so everyone can enjoy themselves.

I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who already enjoys the extraction shooter genre, and it can also be a great starting off point for people new to the genre as well. I can't wait to see what the future holds for Duckov!

Escape from Duckov is a top-down PvE extraction shooter in which you play as a duck and you need to find a way out of this egg-shaped planet.

Simple in essence but very complex in its sytems. Duckov is, in my opinion, the only extraction shooter that manages to come close to what Tarkov offers in terms of core gameplay and character progression. Here, you will be:

- Upgrading your character;
- Building and improving your workstations, allowing your vendors to provide better items;
- Looting every single container you can find and taking pretty much every little item with you;
- Shooting ducks in the face because you're not losing that rare item you just obtained.

The game manages to provide you with some of the best things an extraction shooter has to offer without the overwhelming pressure of losing everything in the blink of an eye as dying just drops a bag you can recover akin to the Souls games... if you want to, that is.

See, Duckov manages to appeal to both more laid-back, casual players and those hardcore ones who would like a far more challenging experience.
The game has several difficulty options, including a fully customizable one that allows you to tailor the experience the way YOU want it to be.

Want something easier and relaxing? Sure, the option is there.
Want enemies to react faster and deal more damage so that any mistake is heavily punished, as well as making so if you die you lose your items? Absolutely, have fun
